newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The economy is on the right road but still needs to be babied along, the government decided at its meeting of the economic team yesterday. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said inflation would continue to fall at a rate of 01.-0.2 percent per month until September and end at around 5.0 percent by the end of the year.
--Private investors have been steadily buying up shares in Greek telecoms organisation's OTE's second share offer. Demand from public subscription is more than double available shares.
--Ten-year fixed-rate bonds to be auctioned on June 17 are expected to draw investor interest, given the attractive interest rate of 8.8 percent.

--The Bank of Greece believes that the reduction of bank operating costs is imperative to close the gap between lending and deposit interest rates, leading to increased forex lending despite a significant fall in drachma interest rates over the past two years.

--A three-year labour market "truce" is on the table in talks between government, unions and employers. According to sources, the truce would monitor wage increases, hours and incentives for new jobs and is supported by senior government members.
--Businesses will be called upon to pay the first trance of the tax on major real estate holdings by August 31. The measure will involve more than 300,000 businesses.
--The finance ministry is planning to enlist the aid of unions in getting major tax evaders to pay off their total 1.6 trillion drachma debt to the state.
--Greece will join Germany, France and Italy in not meeting Maastrict criteria on the public deficit this year, OECD says.
--The pharmaceutical industry is facing a cut of 4-10.0 percent in profits, according to reports. The government is expected to announce measures today.
--OECD warned that containing Greece's public deficit would need work: it estimated that GDP growth would stand at 6.0 percent this year. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
